title: Bristol Pub Quiz

questions.q: Which engineer designed the Clifton Suspension Bridge?
Which Brunel steamship, launched in 1843, is now a museum in a Bristol dry dock?
Which river runs through the gorge beneath the Clifton Suspension Bridge?
In 1497 John Cabot sailed from Bristol to North America aboard which ship?
The Bristol studio Aardman created which inventor and his clever dog?
Which Bristol act released the 1991 album Blue Lines?
Which anonymous street artist, whose early work appeared on Bristol walls in the 1990s, has never confirmed their identity?
Which Hollywood star of North by Northwest was born Archibald Leach in Bristol?
Bristol Rovers are one of the city's professional football clubs. Which is the other?
Every August, hundreds of hot-air balloons lift off from Ashton Court for which event?

notes: Designed by Brunel (winning design, 1831), completed 1864 after his death; see Clifton Suspension Bridge (Wikipedia) or the Clifton Suspension Bridge Trust.
SS Great Britain launched 1843, now a museum ship in the Great Western Dockyard, Bristol; see SS Great Britain (Wikipedia) or ssgreatbritain.org.
The Avon Gorge carries the River Avon beneath the bridge; see Avon Gorge (Wikipedia).
Cabot's 1497 voyage from Bristol on the Matthew; see John Cabot and Matthew (ship) on Wikipedia.
Aardman Animations is based in Bristol and created Wallace and Gromit; see Aardman Animations (Wikipedia).
Blue Lines (1991) is Massive Attack's debut album; the band formed in Bristol; see Blue Lines and Massive Attack (Wikipedia).
Banksy's early work was in Bristol's 1990s underground scene and his identity is unconfirmed; see Banksy (Wikipedia).
Cary Grant born Archibald Alec Leach in Horfield, Bristol, 1904; starred in North by Northwest (1959); see Cary Grant (Wikipedia).
Bristol City play at Ashton Gate, Bristol Rovers at the Memorial Stadium; see Bristol City F.C. and Bristol Rovers F.C. (Wikipedia).
Bristol International Balloon Fiesta held each August at Ashton Court; see Bristol International Balloon Fiesta (Wikipedia) or bristolballoonfiesta.co.uk.
